sections.description: Configuration options for the evaluation framework.

The model every call runs on unless a crew names a profile: the provider follows from `BaseUrl`, then from the model's name, then from the shape of the key. Without this section a host runs on the echo provider, and says so once.
What the log of LLM exchanges keeps of each request and response — read with `--llm-log` only, which says where the log goes.
Configuration options for cost tracking and budget management. Bind to "Orkeon:CostTracking" configuration section.
Configuration options for token counting approximation. Bind to "Orkeon:TokenCounter" configuration section.

The host's caps on model requests — the `RateLimiting` section. Every model call of the host counts, once, at the entrance of its provider: an agent's turns, the manager, the planner, the RAG pipeline, the judges, the cognitive memory, a script's `ctx.llm`. Embeddings do not.
Configuration options for token budget tracking and limits.
Configuration options for tool invocation rate limiting.

The root `Memory` section: the TYPE of the application-wide memory provider, whose connection comes from that provider's own section (`Orkeon:Redis`, …). Bound and judged at the host's start by `AddOrkeonInfrastructure()`: a type the factory does not serve, or one whose section lacks what it needs, refuses the start.
Configuration options for the ChromaDB memory provider. Targets the ChromaDB REST API v2 (servers ≥ 0.6.x, including 1.x); the legacy `/api/v1` surface was removed by recent ChromaDB releases.
Configuration options for the cognitive memory system.

The bounds of what a crew recalls before each task, bound to the `CrewMemoryOptions.SectionName` section by `AddOrkeonInfrastructure()`. A crew with `memory: true` recalls at most `CrewMemoryOptions.RecallLimit` of its memories, those whose cosine similarity to the task reaches `CrewMemoryOptions.MinScore`, cut to `CrewMemoryOptions.MaxChars` characters in all.
Configuration options for the embedding cache.
Configuration options for embedding providers.
Configuration options for AES-256-GCM encryption.

Configuration options for the LanceDB memory provider, backed by a remote LanceDB Cloud / Enterprise server speaking the Lance REST Namespace protocol (`https://docs.lancedb.com/api-reference/rest/`).
Configuration options for the Pinecone memory provider, bound from the host's `Orkeon:Pinecone` section.

Connection options of the Redis memory provider, bound from the host's `Orkeon:Redis` section. Every path that selects Redis by type — the application-wide `Memory:Provider`, a crew's `memoryProvider:`, `Orkeon:Rag:Provider`, `AddOrkeonRedisMemory` — connects with these.
Configuration options for the SQLite memory provider.
Configuration options for vector similarity search.

Complete configuration tree of the RAG query pipeline, bound from the `Orkeon:Rag` configuration section. A `RagOptions.Profile` selects a preset (`RagProfilePresets`); every value can then be overridden individually through configuration — profile = preset, configuration = override.
Options of the `DefaultIngestionPipeline`. Bound from configuration section `Orkeon:Rag:Ingestion` by `AddOrkeonRag`.

Adaptive-RAG query-routing configuration, bound from the `Orkeon:Rag:QueryRouting` configuration section. Selects the `IQueryComplexityClassifier` implementation used to route queries (`NoRetrieval` / `SingleShot` / `Iterative`).

Hybrid-retrieval options, bound from the `Orkeon:Rag:Retrieval:Hybrid` configuration section. The shorthand flat value `Orkeon:Rag:Retrieval:Hybrid = true` is also accepted and maps to `HybridRetrievalOptions.Enabled`.

Transport options of the opt-in RAG web search fallback: endpoint, authentication, timeout and suspicious-content policy of `WebSearchDocumentRetriever`. Standalone options class bound on `Orkeon:Rag:WebFallback` — intentionally NOT part of `RagOptions` to keep the web egress surface a separate, explicit opt-in. Disabled by default; an enabled fallback without an endpoint is treated as disabled and loudly logged.
Configuration options for the code sandbox. Bound from configuration section "Orkeon:CodeSandbox".
Configuration options specific to the Docker sandbox.
Configuration options for the virtual file system. Bound from the "Orkeon:FileSystem" configuration section.
Configuration options for the sandbox virtual file system mount. Bind from the "Orkeon:Sandbox" configuration section.
Configuration options for path security validation.
Configuration options for the DLP system.

Configuration options for the guardian system, bound from `Orkeon:Guardian`. The guardian is on by default: it blocks High and Critical findings only and never rewrites content. A block or a warning is logged and written to the audit trail (`Security:Audit`).
The permission gate of tool calls: off, every call runs. On, a tool that only reads passes and the others need an approval, by permission mode.

A secret by its name — `Secrets:TAVILY_API_KEY` —, where the secret chain looks after the `ORKEON_<NAME>` environment variable and before a vault. A value written here is in clear in the settings file.
Configuration options for the audit trail system.
Configuration options for prompt security and injection detection.

Configuration options for tool result sanitization (`Security:ToolResults`). The length of a result is bounded by one rule only, `AgentDefaults.ResolveMaxToolResultLength`, applied by the tool-invocation pipeline before this sanitizer runs.
Configuration options for URL security validation to prevent SSRF attacks.
Configuration options for secret vault providers.
The key of the Brave Search API. Set — here or as the environment variable of the same name —, it registers the `brave_search` tool; left out, the tool is not offered.
Top-level MCP configuration options: the client's. No option starts the server — `AddOrkeonMcpServer` registers it and `orkeon mcp serve` runs it.
Configuration for the Orkeon MCP server.
Configuration options for multi-modal content support.

The `Orkeon:Tools:Email` section, bound by `EmailOptionsBinder`. Nothing here is validated at bind time, and binding never throws: an account is checked when a tool or a command first uses it, so a broken e-mail section never breaks a crew that sends no mail.

The `Orkeon:Tools:Shell` section: what `ShellCommandTool` may run. Bound by `AddOrkeonCodeTools` and validated when a host starts — an `AllowInterpreters` the binder cannot convert used to surface when the registry built the tool, an unhandled exception out of `--list-tools`.

Options controlling plugin discovery and loading. Bound from the `"Plugins"` configuration section by the `AddOrkeonPlugins(IFileSystemService, IConfiguration)` overload, or configured through the `Action<OrkeonPluginsOptions>` delegate overload.

The semantic index of a codebase and its tools (`index_codebase`, `codebase_search`, `symbol_detail`…). What an index covers — languages, exclusions, root alias — is an argument of each `index_codebase` call, never a setting.
Configuration options for `PostgresStateStore`.
Options for configuring the consensual process strategy.
The switches of the crew factory a shipped host reads.
Options controlling durable persistence of crew execution states (`ScopedCrewExecutionStateManager` → `IStateStore`).
Whether the interactive console prints a model's answer as it arrives.
Full appsettings binding for the CLI scripted-commands subsystem (spec §6.4). Bound to the `Orkeon:Cli:ScriptCommands` section by `ScriptingCliServiceCollectionExtensions.AddScriptCommands`.

Options for `ScriptHostFacade` — chiefly the virtual directories scanned for `<name>/crew.ork.ts` crews. The host populates `ScriptHostFacadeOptions.CrewDirectories` from its mount bootstrap; empty means no crews are resolvable.

The `Orkeon:Cli:Session` section: what a session budgets against. Bound and judged at the host's start by `AddOrkeonSessionTools` — `token_budget` used to read it at each call and fall back on its default, in silence, for a value it could not read.
Sandboxing limits applied to every script engine. Bound to the `Orkeon:Scripting:Limits` configuration section.

Toolchain settings for the scripting runtime. Bound to the `Orkeon:Scripting:Toolchain` configuration section by `ScriptingToolchainOptions.FromConfiguration`, which every host that builds an `EsbuildTranspiler` goes through (`EsbuildTranspiler.Create`).
Top-level A2A protocol configuration options (section `A2A`). Calling `AddOrkeonA2A` is what turns the protocol on; `A2AOptions.EnableServer` adds the hosted server on top of the client stack.
Security options for A2A protocol communications, including mTLS configuration.
Configuration options for Azure AD authentication.
Configuration options for generic OIDC authentication.
The logs of the host:.NET's logging configuration. A shipped host logs warnings and above on one line; `--verbose` raises the level for a run without touching this section.
Configuration options for the monitoring backend. Bind to `Orkeon:Monitoring` in appsettings.json.
Configuration options for Orkeon telemetry. Bind from the "Telemetry" section in appsettings.json.

When a file `Data Source` is supplied, its path is resolved and validated through the virtual file system before being handed to Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, so it must point at a writable VFS mount.

Citation markers stay rank-based (`[1]` = best chunk) whatever the layout.

settings.description: Whether the answer is verified against the retrieved context after generation. Requires an `IGroundednessChecker` registration; enabled without one, the stage is traced as skipped.

The host LLM profile (`Llm:Profiles:<name>`) every model call of the subsystem goes to — grounded generation, the query transformers, the listwise reranker, the corrective graph's evaluator and groundedness checker, the `llm` classifier and the evaluation judge. Null, blank or `default` is the host's default profile. A host key: one profile for the whole subsystem, which no preset sets.

Profile name (`fast`, `balanced`, `quality`, `adaptive`, `corrective`). Defaults to `RagDefaults.DefaultProfile` (`fast` — `balanced` needs the opt-in ONNX reranker package). Unknown names fail loudly.

Gets or sets the memory-provider type backing the RAG document store: `inmemory`, `in-memory`, `redis`, `sqlite`, `chromadb`, `chroma`, `pinecone`, `lancedb`, `lance`. `null` or empty selects the ambient container provider.
Transformer name resolved through the query-transformer factory: `none` (default), `multi-query`, `rag-fusion` or `hyde`. `none` skips the stage; unknown names fail loudly.
Number of variants requested from non-`none` transformers.

Default number of chunks kept after reranking (a call-site `RagQuery.TopN` wins).

settings.description: Number of candidates retrieved before fusion/rerank (wide stage of the 50 → 5 cascade). The pipeline always retrieves at least the final TopN.

Relevance/diversity trade-off in `[0, 1]`: `1` keeps the pure relevance order, `0` maximises diversity. Defaults to `MmrOptions.DefaultLambda`.

Chunking strategy resolved by the chunking factory when an `IngestionRequest` names none. Defaults to `recursive`.

Virtual directory (VFS path) holding the per-collection ingestion manifests (`{collection}.json`). Defaults to `/output/rag/manifests` — under the conventional writable `/output` mount, next to other run artifacts.

Classifier name: `QueryRoutingOptions.HeuristicClassifier` (default — safe, deterministic, works without any LLM) or `QueryRoutingOptions.LlmClassifier`. Unknown names fail loudly at resolution. When `llm` is selected but no `IChatClient` is registered, the heuristic classifier is used as the documented fallback (with a warning) rather than failing.

Explicit, noisy opt-in to allow executing code on a sandbox that provides NO OS-level isolation (the host process runner) when an isolating sandbox (Docker) is unavailable. Default is `false` (fail-closed): if no OS-isolating sandbox is available, code execution is REFUSED rather than silently falling back to the host. Set this to `true` only for trusted, non-LLM code in a trusted environment — it is RCE-equivalent on the host.

Infrastructure mounts, same grammar as `FileSystemOptions.Mounts`, registered with `MountVisibility.Internal`: resolvable, but absent from `GetAvailableMounts()` and therefore from `list_mounts`, the agent prompt's mount table and access-denied messages. This is where a runner puts what it needs the VFS to reach but no agent has any business addressing — the LLM exchange log directory, for one. The mount-string grammar has no room for a visibility token, which is why this is a separate list rather than a fourth field. A boundary, not just a hiding place. The `IFileSystemService` every tool holds refuses these mounts, and reports them exactly like a path that does not exist. Infrastructure that must reach one asks for `PrivilegedFileSystemAccess` by name. It used to be a hiding place — resolvable for anyone who typed the name, and the names are documented — so a single `file_read /llm-logs/…` handed an agent every prompt of the run.
Mount definitions in the format "physical:virtual:rights[;subpath:rights;...]".
Age threshold for orphaned session directories. Directories older than this value are deleted by the janitor on startup. Defaults to 24 hours.

The policy the Guardian's input phase applies to the composed user prompt. Default `SanitizationPolicy.Block`: a High or Critical pattern fails the task before any provider call, a lower one is logged and audited; the prompt is never rewritten.

The policy applied to a successful tool result. Default `SanitizationPolicy.Warn`: the result reaches the model tagged as data and any injection pattern is logged and audited. `SanitizationPolicy.Block` withholds a result carrying a High or Critical pattern (the model is told so); `SanitizationPolicy.None` passes results untouched and untagged.

Tools whose results bypass sanitization. Defaults to the `email_*` tools, which screen what they read with `PromptInjectionDocumentValidator` and mark it untrusted themselves (ADR-012) — tagging them again would stack two envelopes. Entries from configuration are added to these.

Microsoft tenant: `consumers` (default), `organizations`, `common` or a tenant id.
Login name; defaults to the address.
Display name paired with `EmailAccountOptions.Address` in `From`.

Server port.
`Imap`, `Pop3` or `Graph`; the preset decides when unset.
Transport security.
Server host name.
Server port.
`Smtp` or `Graph`; the preset decides when unset.
Transport security.
The preset: `Gmail`, `Outlook` or `Custom` (the default).
What an agent may do, e.g. `"Read, Organize, Draft"`. Mandatory.
Whether a sent message is appended to the Sent folder. Unset follows the preset: Gmail, Outlook and Graph file sent mail themselves, a custom server usually does not.
Who may receive mail from this account: an address, `*@domain`, or `*` for anyone. Empty means nobody: sending is closed until an operator opens it.
Most messages this process sends per hour from the account. Unset means no cap.
Most recipients one message may have. Unset leaves the limit to the server.
Protocol timeout in seconds. Unset keeps the library default.
Physical directory holding the OAuth tokens, for a host whose per-user settings directory is not the right one (a service account). Read by the host, not by the tools.
The account a call uses when it names none. Optional with a single account.
When true, a message the prompt-injection detector rejects has its body withheld. Off by default: the detector was tuned on web pages, and newsletters trip it.
A full replacement of the default allowlist, verbatim; it cancels `ShellToolOptions.AllowInterpreters` and re-enables the git read-only restriction. Empty keeps the default allowlist.
Enables the interpreters (`node`, `dotnet`, `npm`, `find`) and the mutating git subcommands — RCE-equivalent on the host, for trusted coding-agent hosts only. Default false.
Commands added on top of the default (or replacement) allowlist, such as `make`.

When `true`, a plugin assembly that fails to load or to configure its services is recorded in `IPluginRegistry.Failures` and the remaining candidates keep loading. When `false` (default), the first failure throws a `PluginLoadException` (fail fast).
Virtual path (VFS) of the directory scanned for plugin assemblies. Must start with `/` and resolve inside a configured mount. Default: `/plugins`.
Simple glob pattern applied to candidate assembly file names (e.g. `*.dll`, `MyCompany.*.dll`). Candidates must additionally carry the `.dll` extension regardless of the pattern. Default: `*.dll`.

Assembly simple-name prefixes that are never loaded into the plugin's isolated `AssemblyLoadContext`; resolution defers to the host (default) context instead, so contract types (e.g. `IOrkeonPlugin`, `IBaseTool`, `IServiceCollection`) keep a single identity shared between the host and the plugin. Defaults: `Orkeon.`, `Orkeon.Rag.Abstractions` and `Microsoft.Extensions.`.
The key of a remote provider. The local provider needs none.
The `http://` or `https://` address of the provider's endpoint, when it is not the provider's own.
The size of the vectors, for a model that lets it be chosen. Left out, the model's own.
The most characters of one text sent to the model; what is longer is cut. Left out, the provider's own limit.
The embedding model. Left out, the provider uses its own — `bge-micro-v2` for the local one.
Who computes the embeddings, any case. The default runs on the machine: no key, no network.
Whether the index and its tools are registered. `false` leaves them out of the host.
Gets or sets whether to auto-create the schema and tables on first use.
Gets or sets the PostgreSQL connection string.
Gets or sets the maximum number of version entries per session (default: 1000).
Gets or sets the schema name (default: "orkeon").
Gets or sets whether discussion rounds are enabled when consensus is not reached. During discussion, agents receive the context of other agents' results.
Gets or sets the fallback strategy when consensus cannot be reached.
Gets or sets the maximum number of voting rounds before applying fallback. A round runs every agent on the task, then collects one ballot per agent.
Gets or sets role-based weights for weighted consensus voting. Key is the agent role, value is the weight multiplier.

Gets or sets whether abstention is allowed. When true (the default), an abstention only counts toward the quorum. When false, an abstention counts as a vote against every choice: it stays in the denominator of each share, and it breaks unanimity. A Borda count, which has no share threshold, then reaches no consensus while anyone abstains.
Gets or sets the consensus threshold percentage. Used by SuperMajority and WeightedConsensus types.
Gets or sets the consensus type to use.
Gets or sets the quorum, in percent: the minimum share of expressed ballots among all ballots. Below it, no consensus is reached, whatever the expressed ballots say.
Gets or sets whether to use weighted votes.

Whether a tool a crew names and the registry does not hold fails the crew's load, listing the unknown names and the available ones. `false` drops the tool with a warning instead — the library's lenient behaviour, which the shipped hosts turn off.

When `true`, archiving an execution (completion or expiry cleanup) also deletes its persisted entry from the state store. Default: `false` — the final snapshot is kept in the store so that status queries keep working after the in-memory entry is evicted.
Enables durable persistence of execution states. Default: `false` (in-memory only, identical to the historical behavior).
Whether each piece of an answer is written to the console as the model sends it, instead of the whole answer at its end.
When false, two scripts declaring the same command name is a fatal startup error.
Virtual paths scanned for `*.cmd.ts`. First directory wins on conflict.
Master switch. False ⇒ discovery is skipped, registry is empty.
When false, `*.cmd.js` only (no TS transpile). Test/debug; production keeps this true.
When true, the first invalid script aborts the loader (use in CI).

Name of the scripted command that handles free text (a REPL line not prefixed with `/`). In the coding-agent surface this is the interactive assistant wired to the `main-loop` crew. Empty/unknown ⇒ free text yields the unknown-command message instead of being routed.
Hard timeout for a single command invocation. Default: 5 minutes.
Memory cap in bytes. Default: 64 MB (spec §8.1 CLI profile).
Recursion depth cap. Default: 100 (inherited from spec §8.1 — same as global).
Hard cap on the number of engines kept in cache.
Virtual directories under which crews live as `<dir>/<name>/crew.ork.ts`. Resolution tries each directory in order; first match wins.
The crew entry-file name resolved under each `<dir>/<name>/`.

Upper bound on a single synchronous `script-host.runCrew` call. When it expires, the calling script receives a clear `TimeoutException`, the abandoned run is cancelled cooperatively, and the engine/REPL thread is always released. Default: 10 minutes — generous on purpose, since `runCrew` is meant for short crews (long workflows should go through `runCrewAsync`'s ticket cycle). Zero or a negative value disables the bound.
The model's context window, in tokens: a number above zero. Unset is `CliSessionOptions.DefaultContextWindowTokens`.

Maximum wall-clock time the engine is allowed to run, in total. Default: 30 seconds — strict `Untrusted` profile. IMPORTANT: this configures Jint's `TimeoutInterval`, which is wall-clock, not JS-bytecode CPU time. Time spent awaiting a C# Task from JS (e.g. `await Tools.indexCodebase(...)`) IS counted — the engine's internal Stopwatch keeps ticking while the host runs async work. This is a security ceiling that bounds how long a hostile script can pin a thread. Trusted long-running design-spec runs must opt in explicitly by raising `Orkeon:Scripting:Limits:ExecutionTimeout` in appsettings. The strict default stays tight. One window per root pump: a crew run the CLR drives (the `globalThis.crew` handoff through `ScriptHost`, `JsCrew.RunAsync`) runs under it from the invocation of the run function to its last settled promise, the way a script already did — not once per agent body — so a host driving a run longer than this raises the limit.

Maximum cumulative memory the engine is allowed to allocate, in bytes. Default: 100 MB — an `Untrusted`-by-default profile for `.ork.ts` scripts of unknown provenance. IMPORTANT: Jint's `LimitMemory` is cumulative, not peak. It uses `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` and counts every allocation since the engine was created — including short-lived intermediates from template-literal concatenation, JSON serialization of tool calls, esbuild bundle parsing, etc. This is a security ceiling that bounds local DoS by a pathological or hostile script. Trusted production runs that genuinely need more memory (e.g. RaggableTree bundling) must opt in explicitly: raise `Orkeon:Scripting:Limits:MemoryLimitBytes` in appsettings, or set `--memory-limit-mb 0` on the CLI (translates to a large ceiling) for a fully trusted run. The strict default stays tight. One window per root pump, like `ScriptingLimitsOptions.ExecutionTimeout`: a crew run the CLR drives (the `globalThis.crew` handoff through `ScriptHost`, `JsCrew.RunAsync`) counts every agent body's allocations against one budget, the way a script already did — not one fresh window per body — so a many-agent run that allocates raises the limit.

Maximum recursion depth before the engine throws. Default: 64 (lowered from 100 for the strict `Untrusted` profile). Catches runaway recursion well before the.NET stack overflow while leaving room for legitimately nested script logic. Trusted scripts may raise it via `Orkeon:Scripting:Limits:RecursionLimit`.

Absolute path to the esbuild binary. When null, the transpiler falls back to the `ORKEON_ESBUILD_PATH` environment variable, then to a binary bundled next to the application (`esbuild-bin/esbuild`), then to a PATH lookup.
Maximum time esbuild has to transpile a single source. Default: 30 s.
The agent description advertised in the agent card.
The agent name advertised in the agent card.
The agent version advertised in the agent card.
Contact URL for the provider field in the agent card.
Whether to run an A2A server exposing local agents for remote task submission: registers `IA2AServer` and a hosted service that starts it with the host.
The host/prefix for the A2A HTTP server (e.g., "http://localhost").
Organization name for the provider field in the agent card.
The port for the A2A HTTP server to listen on.
Timeout in seconds for outbound HTTP requests to remote agents.

Authentication schemes the server accepts on its task endpoints: `Bearer` and/or `ApiKey`. Empty means no authentication is required. Each declared scheme is validated, not merely matched (`A2ACredentialValidator`): a bearer token by a registered `IAuthenticationProvider` (`A2A:Security:AzureAD` / `A2A:Security:Oidc`), an API key against `A2ASecurityOptions.ApiKeySecretNames`. The server refuses to start when a declared scheme has no validator.

Names of the secrets holding the API keys the `ApiKey` scheme accepts (`Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Each name is read through the `ISecretProvider` on every request — `ORKEON_<NAME>` with the default chain — so keys never sit in the configuration file and rotate without a restart.

Client side: the scheme of the credential the client sends on every task call (`Authorization: <scheme> <credential>`) — `Bearer` or `ApiKey`, matching what the peer declares in its `A2ASecurityOptions.AllowedAuthSchemes`. Empty means the client sends no `Authorization` header. Agent-card discovery never carries it.
Password for the client certificate private key.
Path to the client certificate file for mTLS authentication.

Client side: name of the secret holding the credential sent with `A2ASecurityOptions.ClientAuthScheme`, read through the `ISecretProvider` on every call (`ORKEON_<NAME>` with the default chain) so it never sits in the configuration file and rotates without a restart. A call fails before any request when it cannot be read.

Whether mTLS is required for server-to-server communication. When enabled, the server requires a client certificate that chains to one of the `A2ASecurityOptions.TrustedCertificateAuthorities` or matches one of the `A2ASecurityOptions.TrustedClientCertificateThumbprints`; starting the server without any configured trust anchor throws (fail-closed) — mere presence and date validity of a certificate is not authentication.

List of trusted certificate authority certificate paths. Client side: when set, only servers presenting certificates signed by these CAs are trusted (private-CA pinning). Server side: when `A2ASecurityOptions.RequireMutualTls` is enabled, incoming client certificates must chain to one of these CAs (unless pinned via `A2ASecurityOptions.TrustedClientCertificateThumbprints`).

Thumbprints (hex, case-insensitive) of client certificates accepted by the server when `A2ASecurityOptions.RequireMutualTls` is enabled — exact pinning, checked before the `A2ASecurityOptions.TrustedCertificateAuthorities` chain validation. Pinned certificates are still rejected outside their validity window.
Authority URL (e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/v2.0).
Application (client) ID registered in Azure AD.
Azure AD tenant ID.
Valid audiences for token validation.
Valid token issuers. Defaults to standard Azure AD issuers for the tenant.
OIDC authority URL (e.g. https://login.example.com/realms/myapp).
Client ID registered with the OIDC provider.
Whether to require HTTPS for the metadata endpoint. Defaults to true.
Valid audiences for token validation.
The console logger's own section: its `LogLevel` by category, `FormatterName`, `FormatterOptions` and the other keys of.NET's console logger.

The lowest level logged, by category: `Default` for every category without a line of its own, a namespace such as `Orkeon.Infrastructure` for what it logs. A level that is none refuses the start, naming the key.
Maximum number of completed traces kept in the circular buffer. Older traces are evicted when this limit is reached.
Number of minutes to retain detailed metrics data.

Prefix of the activity-source names whose traces are captured. Defaults to every Orkeon source; narrow it to watch one subsystem — or, in a test, to a name nothing else emits, since the listener is process-wide and would otherwise pick up unrelated activity.
Gets or sets whether telemetry is enabled. Default is true.
Gets or sets the maximum memory threshold in MB for health checks. Default is 2048 MB.

Gets or sets the OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) exporter endpoint. When set, traces and metrics are exported to this endpoint. Example: "http://localhost:4317" for gRPC or "http://localhost:4318" for HTTP.
